newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. aid chief appeals for $126 million for N.Korea.
newsitem.headline: U.N. aid chief appeals for $126 million for N.Korea.

text.p: The United Nations on Monday launched an appeal for $126.2 million for North Korea to stave off an imminent famine over the next few months.

Most of the funds, $95 million, are for food supplies and were announced last week by the World Food Programme. The additional monies requested cover programmes from other U.N. agencies over the next year.
"The situation can be described as a humantarian disaster in the making," said Yasushi Akashi, head of the Department of Humanitarian Affairs (DHA), at a news conference.

In addition to the badly-needed food aid, the appeal includes $10 million for the Food and Agriculture Organisation, $4.7 million for the U.N. Children's Fund, $9.8 million for the U.N. Development Programme, $5.5 million for the World Health Organisation and $75,000 for the DHA itself.

The money is sought for projects on future crop production, including seeds, fertiliser and animal husbandry projects. It is also targeting 300 nurseries and kindergartens as well as health clinics desperately short of medicines.
The appeal said that the lack of food has weakened the immune systems of thousands of people and exposed the general population, particularly children, to epidemics.

In visits to Pyongyang and three southern agricultural counties in March, World Food Programme inspectors found signs that even the most marginal measures to deal with two consecutive years of crop-killing floods were breaking down.
Children were malnourished and many were stunted while the populace in general was living on rations of 3.5 ounces (100 grams) of rice per day, or about one bowlful.
People survived on this rice, plus stores of dried vegetable leaves, ground corncobs and ground sweet potato stalks, they said.
